prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent watercolour washes over it, a muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a thoughtful printed picture book for adults. NOT neon, NOT 3D or CGI or Pixar, NOT glossy plastic, NOT neo-comic, NOT photoreal. PORTRAIT BOOK COVER.

A warm ordinary family-house room at dusk, seen from inside. In the LOWER THIRD, small and seen from behind and slightly to one side, MARCUS sits at a plain wooden desk: a man in his late thirties in a soft OLIVE-GREEN open shirt over a grey tee, wire-rimmed glasses pushed up into his short dark hair.

In front of him on the desk stands THE SUPERCHARGED LAPTOP, and it fills the middle of the cover. THE ENTIRE LAPTOP IS A TRANSLUCENT LUMINOUS HOLOGRAPHIC OBJECT GLOWING WARM AMBER-ORANGE, glowing all through its lid, keyboard, base and edges, so you can see through the whole machine. It casts warm light into the room rather than shadow. Its screen face is toward the viewer.

INSIDE the screen, opening away into impossible depth, is a small bright LINE OF STATIONS receding into the distance, with tiny glowing rounded mascot figures working at little desks along it, passing a book from one to the next. The factory is entirely inside the machine. The room around it is ordinary: a shelf of children's picture books, a mug, a child's crayon drawing taped to the wall.

BAKED TITLE LETTERING integrated at the TOP of the cover in a warm hand-lettered serif in deep ink brown, reading EXACTLY and ONLY: 'What a Book Is Made Of'. Below it, much smaller, in small caps, reading EXACTLY and ONLY: 'A HYPERAGENTIC AGE story'. NO other text, no author name, no publisher, no taglines, no invented words, no numbers. Spell both strings perfectly.

ONE single continuous full-bleed painting. Never a grid, never panels.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
